newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore renews magazine permit after lewd ads cut.
newsitem.headline: Singapore renews magazine permit after lewd ads cut.

text.p: The Singapore government said on Tuesday it has renewed the publication licence of a magazine, reversing an earlier decision not to renew the permit due to government objections to lewd advertisements.
"It is confirmed that we have renewed the licence," a spokesman for the Ministry of Information and the Arts (MITA) said.
The renewal followed IS Magazine's agreement to adhere to strict guidelines and will come into effect on July 12.
The spokesman said MITA had considered the appeal from the free fortnightly publication to renew its permit and had informed the publisher.
MITA said early this month that IS Magazine flouted publishing guidelines issued by the ministry by printing objectionable items. The magazine's permit was not renewed when it expired on June 12.
It was found to have published telephone numbers offering phone sex, lewd ads and ads which promoted homosexuality.

The spokesman said the ministry decided to renew the licence after a meeting with the magazine's publisher and staff, who gave an assurance that the personal advertisement column would be dropped and guidelines on sexual content in local publications would be adhered to.

"The decision was made following a meeting with IS Magazine, when IS gave an assurance that stringent editorial control will be exercised over the magazine to ensure no flouting of the ministry's guidelines in future," the spokesman said, in a written reply to queries from Reuters.
"We are certain that the magazine can be interesting without going donwstream," the spokesman said.
Singapore practises censorship and imposes restrictions on the media in various areas to protect what it views as basic values.
Certain magazines such as Playboy, Penthouse and Cosmopolitan are not allowed in the city state.
The publisher of IS magazine Gretchen Worth could not be immediately reached for comment.
The magazine earlier confirmed it had appealed against the action and was confident its agreement to remove the ads would comply with most of MITA's objections.
IS Magazine is published by Hong Kong-based company Asia City Publishing Group and has an audited circulation of 25,000.
